feature: Switching the history filter is instant
summary: Switching All, Screenshots and Videos in the history bar now swaps the strip in one frame, even with 500 captures, and a switch from far along lands at the start at once. Every tile now keeps a small picture made in the background instead of the whole screenshot.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Best with a big Screenshots folder (yours had about 500 on 2026-09-30).

try.do: Press Shift-Command-H to open the history bar.
Click Screenshots, then Videos, then All, a few times over.
Press the right arrow twenty or thirty times to walk well along the strip.
Click Videos: the strip should show the newest recordings at the start, with no scroll back.
Close the bar and open it again: tiles already seen appear at once.

evaluate: Does a filter switch now feel instant to you, with the chip and the new set arriving together?
Does a tile you have not seen yet appear quickly enough when it fades in from grey?
Is jumping straight to the start after a switch from far along what you want, rather than keeping your place?
Do the thumbnails look as sharp as before, in the bar and on the capture card?
rough: Measured in the loop's copy of the app. On your own Screenshots folder, before: opening the bar froze for up to 320ms and the first switch for 45ms. After: opening 135ms and every switch 3 to 11ms. On a made-up folder of 500 captures, a switch from far along went from 126ms to 8ms, and repeat switches rebuild at most 1 tile.

Opening the bar still stalls for about 125 to 135ms in one pass. On the made-up folder it did that before this change too, so what is left is the bar itself, not the pictures. Not filed yet: it is outside this task, and it is written in this task's log.
The very first click on the bar still costs one frame of about 20ms whatever it clicks: that is the bar taking the keyboard, not the filter.
The first time a recording is ever shown, its first Videos switch can take one pass of about 17ms while its poster is made. After that the poster comes from a small cache on disk.
Walking the strip with the arrow keys still costs about a tenth of a second per step. It was the same before this change, and it is filed on its own.
The segmented chip takes one more pass of 15 to 20ms just after each move, even with the strip left unchanged. That is logged on the chip's own task.
No mock page draws the history bar. Its look is unchanged apart from a grey placeholder that fades to the picture.
